Together, these passages substantiate the core of the control assertion that admin functions are gated by an is_admin flag and that admins have global read/write capabilities. However, the limitation that administrators have global access "without finer-grained roles or scoping" goes beyond what is written; the documentation does not state whether additional role or scope controls exist, so that part is an inference from silence. ### Identity Service

Authenticates customers, drivers, and staff. All interactive sign-in is delegated to the
company's SSO provider over OpenID Connect; the service issues short-lived internal tokens
that the core services verify.

The single public entry point. It terminates TLS, authenticates every request against the
Identity Service, applies per-client rate limits, and routes to the core services.

assessments.rationale: evd-001 establishes that Parcelworks serves customers (plural). evd-002 shows that drivers use the Mobile Gateway via the API Gateway to send scan events and proof-of-delivery photos. evd-003 and evd-004 document that tracking data and proof-of-delivery photos are maintained in back-end stores such as the Tracking Store and Object Storage. Together, these passages support the applicability_reason's claim that a compromised driver account could, in principle, affect tracking data held in shared back-end stores, making a tenant- or customer-aware authorization requirement (req-AUTHZ-001) relevant to the scenario in general. The documentation, however, does not describe any tenant- or customer-specific authorization checks on driver actions, nor does it define threat thr-002 or the precise semantics of req-AUTHZ-001. The mapping's conclusion that the requirement is applicable to thr-002 and currently "unverified" is therefore only partially supported: applicability at a high level is well supported, while the threat-specific mapping and the assessment status depend on requirement and threat definitions not present in the evidence.
